teachersDay.title: Teachers’ Day 2026 at ITHS: A Celebration Planned by Students
teachersDay.html:
The Institute of Translational Health Science (ITHS) celebrated Teachers’ Day 2026 on 3rd September 2026 with great enthusiasm and reverence, recognising the dedication, mentorship, and invaluable contributions of its faculty members and Heads of Departments.

The Students Took Charge

The celebration was organised entirely by the students of ITHS. They planned the programme, arranged the activities, and kept the preparations a surprise for their teachers until the day itself. That students put so much thought and effort into an afternoon meant for someone else was, in itself, the warmest tribute of the day.

An Afternoon of Performances, Quizzes, and Games

The programme brought faculty and students together for an engaging afternoon filled with cultural performances, interactive activities, games, and memorable moments.

Students opened with performances that drew warm applause from the faculty. A KBC-inspired quiz followed, putting teachers and students in the hot seat together and turning the usual classroom dynamic upside down for an hour. Faculty-student activities and a lively Musical Chairs session had everyone on their feet, with the teachers joining in as enthusiastically as their students and creating an atmosphere of camaraderie and celebration.

Cake, Tokens of Appreciation, and a Faculty Lunch

The event concluded with a cake-cutting ceremony and the presentation of tokens of appreciation to the teachers, followed by a special faculty lunch. The thoughtful efforts of the students and the enthusiastic participation of the faculty made the celebration a memorable occasion for everyone present.

A Bond That Goes Beyond the Classroom

The celebration reflected the strong teacher-student bond at ITHS and reaffirmed the institute’s commitment to fostering a culture of respect, gratitude, and collaborative learning.

Days like this one matter because they change the register of the relationship for a few hours. Students see their teachers laugh, compete, and lose gracefully at Musical Chairs. Teachers see the care and organisation their students are capable of when nobody has assigned it to them. Everyone returns to class a little more at ease with one another, and that ease is what makes students comfortable enough to ask questions.

Thank You to Our Teachers

Teachers’ Day served as a meaningful reminder of the vital role educators play in inspiring students, nurturing their potential, and shaping the professionals and leaders of tomorrow. ITHS extends its heartfelt gratitude to every faculty member and Head of Department for their guidance, patience, and commitment, and to the students whose efforts made the day so memorable.

orientation.title: Orientation cum Induction Programme 2026: Welcoming Our New Batch at ITHS, Rayat Bahra University
orientation.html:
Every academic journey has a beginning, and for the newest members of the Institute of Translational Health Science (ITHS) family, that beginning arrived with the Orientation cum Induction Programme 2026. Held at Rayat Bahra University, Chandigarh, the event brought together new students, faculty, and staff for a day filled with warmth, energy, and purpose.

Setting the Tone for a New Academic Year

The Orientation cum Induction Programme is more than a formal welcome, it’s the first real introduction students get to life at ITHS. This year’s edition was designed to do exactly that: familiarize new students with the institute’s academic environment, walk them through the departments and laboratories they’ll come to know well, and introduce the support systems in place to help them thrive from day one.

From the moment students walked in, the goal was clear. Make them feel like they already belonged.

A Programme Built on Teamwork

None of this comes together without people working quietly and effectively behind the scenes. The organizing team’s coordination was evident throughout the day, and that same spirit of collaboration is really what ITHS is built on.

A few teams deserve a special shoutout:

  • Stage Management & Student Engagement Team, for curating interactive activities that kept students genuinely involved rather than just watching from the sidelines.
  • Discipline Management Team, for ensuring the event ran smoothly, with excellent coordination that often goes unnoticed but never goes unappreciated.
  • Administrative, Accounts, and Logistics Teams, for handling everything from seating arrangements to hall decoration, making sure students felt comfortable the moment they arrived.

Hands-On from Day One: Laboratory Exposure Sessions

One of the highlights of the programme was the laboratory exposure sessions, giving new students an early, up-close look at the institute’s practical and research facilities. For a health science institute, this kind of firsthand exposure matters, it turns an abstract idea of “what I’ll be studying” into something tangible students can see and connect with right away.

Paired with the welcoming and introductory sessions, the day struck a nice balance between structure and warmth, informative enough to set expectations, and welcoming enough to ease any first-day nerves.

More Than Just an Event

By the time the programme concluded, it had done what it set out to do: introduce students to their new academic home while building a genuine sense of belonging, motivation, and excitement for what’s ahead.

At ITHS, this is really the foundation of everything. A supportive, research-driven, student-centered environment where new students aren’t just enrolled. They’re welcomed.

Here’s to the new batch and everything they’ll go on to achieve. Welcome to ITHS!

Institute of Translational Health Science (ITHS), Rayat Bahra University, Chandigarh
